content:
PURPOSE:
Quick prep notes for the Aurora Pay escalation war-room (scheduled 2026-04-18 09:30 PT). Personal scratchpad to take into the meeting and capture live action items.

AGENDA (30m):
- 09:30-09:35 quick context + current customer impact (Sofia)
- 09:35-09:45 incident timeline & telemetry deep-dive (Ravi)
- 09:45-09:55 mitigation options and immediate steps (Eng on-call: Hannah)
- 09:55-10:05 escalation path / customer comms (CS lead: Sofia, AE: Jamal)
- 10:05-10:15 confirmed action owners & timings, next check-in cadence

ATTENDEES (invited):
- Aurora Pay: Lina Wu (SRE), Marco Diaz (Engineering Manager)
- Redwood: Sofia Martinez (CS lead), Ravi Singh (observability), Hannah Lee (on-call eng), Jamal Ortiz (AE), Priya Kapoor (support)

SUMMARY OF ISSUE (short):
- Since 2026-04-17 22:10 UTC Aurora observed elevated 5xx rates and intermittent timeouts for Redwood-hosted payment routing endpoint used in their realtime fraud checks.
- Customer reports spike correlates with peak batch job at 22:00 UTC. Their SLA demands P95 latency < 300ms for tokenized lookup calls; currently P95 ~ 1.2s and error rate ~ 6% (baseline < 0.2%).
- Customer is on a Dedicated instance (reserved capacity) with autoscale disabled; running a quantized model variant (q4) for routing.

WHAT WE KNOW (telemetry):
- Error breakdown (last 60m): 70% upstream 502 from inference backend, 20% gateway timeouts, 10% application-level rejects (rate limiter).
- Infra metrics: GPU utilization on dedicated pool node group peaked at 94% at 22:03 UTC; queue depth increased from ~30 -> 420.
- Batching metrics: average batch size doubled vs normal (indicates sudden request bursts from customer's side).
- KV cache hit rate dropped from 82% -> 34% during spike (possible shifting prefix patterns).
- No config changes by Redwood on 2026-04-17 in that region; Aurora ran a data backfill job at 22:00 UTC (their note).

INITIAL HYPOTHESIS:
1) Customer job created a short-lived high QPS burst that saturated dedicated GPUs; runtime batching increased latency and caused gateway upstream 502s.
2) KV cache invalidation or poor prefix locality during the job reduced cache benefits, increasing per-request compute.
3) Because autoscale is off for this Dedicated contract, fallback to hosted pool did not occur; requests queued and timed out.

IMMEDIATE MITIGATION OPTIONS (fast, temporary):
- Option A (recommended short-term): Temporarily enable burst autoscaling for Aurora's dedicated pool (add 1-2 nodes) to relieve saturation. Requires infra approval and ~10-15min to provision. (Owner: Hannah)
- Option B: Strict rate limiting on high-cost routes for Aurora for 15m to smooth bursts; coordinate with Aurora to pause non-essential jobs. (Owner: Priya)
- Option C: Route subset of traffic to a verified compatible hosted model variant that has spare capacity to handle async fraud checks. Needs customer approval for data routing. (Owner: Sofia + Jamal)

COMMUNICATION PLAN (what we tell customer now):
- Acknowledge: "We see elevated errors/latency, investigating root cause. Our immediate plan is to add capacity and apply temporary throttles on non-critical jobs. We'll update in 15 minutes and share a postmortem."
- Avoid technical blame; propose concrete short-term steps and expected timeline (15m, 60m, 24h).

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS TO COVER IN WAR-ROOM:
- Can Aurora pause their 22:00 backfill for the next 24h? If not, we need a long-term solution (autoscale or capacity bump).
- If we enable burst nodes, are there quota limits in their region for additional GPUs? (Infra check)
- Any PII/data residency concerns if we route traffic to hosted pool? (Security check)
- Could model variant incompatibility cause silent higher compute per request? Need model profiler check. (Applied ML)

SCRIPTS / QUICK COMMANDS TO RUN (ops):
- Check nodegroup GPU saturation: k8s namespace/redwood-dedicated aurora-pay -> kubectl top nodes / describe pod (Ravi/Hannah)
- Check gateway logs for 502 trace ids: splunk query: source=gateway aurora-pay 502 | top trace_id (Ravi)
- Temporarily increase dedicated pool nodes: infra-runbook/lift-burst-autoscale --customer aurora-pay --count 2 (Hannah)

ACTION ITEMS (captured live during meeting) - DRAFT (fill owners/due):
- AH1: Enable burst autoscale + monitor error rate (Owner: Hannah) - due: 2026-04-18 09:45 PT
- AH2: Apply short-term rate limit on non-critical endpoints and inform Aurora (Owner: Priya) - due: 2026-04-18 09:40 PT
- AH3: Validate KV cache performance and run model profiler to check per-token compute changes (Owner: Ravi + Applied ML) - due: 2026-04-18 12:00 PT
- AH4: Draft customer-facing status update and confirm routing option to hosted pool with legal/security checklist (Owner: Sofia + Jamal) - due: 2026-04-18 09:50 PT
- AH5: Check region GPU quota for Aurora's project; escalate with infra if limited (Owner: Hannah) - due: 2026-04-18 10:00 PT

NOTES TO SELF / MEETING TRICKS:
- Keep language action-oriented; customers want timelines.
- If Aurora resists routing to hosted pool, offer a short-term contract amendment for temporary capacity.
- Capture trace-ids for any 502s and attach to Jira CS-2345 for the postmortem.

POST-MEETING (what to include in follow-up doc):
- Timeline of events + key metrics (P95, 5xx, queue depth) before/during/after mitigation
- Action item table with owners and completion timestamps
- Root cause analysis and long-term remediation plan (autoscale policy change or dedicated capacity increase)
- Customer communications log and any legal/PII considerations

MISC / SCRATCH (questions I want to ask during war-room):
- Was there any internal rollout or model swap on 2026-04-17 that affected quantization profile? (check release-engineering)
- Can we enable a temporary fallback policy in routing rules that bypasses queueing for critical endpoints?

BOTTOM LINE (prep):
- Primary ask: get capacity relief on the Dedicated pool now (burst nodes) + immediate rate smoothing.
- Secondary: validate cache/model behaviour; agree with Aurora on preventing the backfill during peak while we finalize autoscale or capacity changes.

---
Scratchpad ends here. Will convert action items to Jira after meeting and move finalized notes to Confluence (linked above).
